You need to be based locally to any of the areas to be considered for the role. Be part of something great Maximus is a global organisation that specialises in providing health and employment services to millions of people every year. Here in the UK we employ around 5,000 people across the country to deliver services that have a profound impact on people’s lives. From assessments and health services to employability programmes and specialist support, we do work that matters with people who care. The Health System Navigator is a non-clinical role that helps participants and delivery teams overcome health-system, community, accessibility and environmental barriers that affect participation and progression towards work. The role builds effective relationships with local health services, local authorities, VCSE organisations, social prescribing, disability, skills and community partners; facilitates warm connections; tracks access; and feeds local-system intelligence into continuous improvement. The Navigator does not clinically assess, diagnose, treat, prescribe, provide therapy or hold clinical risk. Participant navigation and access support Support participants where progression is affected by system, access, communication, service or environmental barriers. Help participants understand available local options and make informed choices about support routes. Facilitate warm introductions, supported self-referrals and practical preparation for service contact through community partnerships & local authority. Track whether contact, attendance and engagement occur and agree alternative routes where needed. Local partnership development Build and maintain relationships with NHS, primary care, community health, local authority, social prescribing, VCSE, disability, skills and community partners. Maintain an accurate local service and community asset map, including eligibility, access routes, waiting times and accessibility options. Develop warm-referral arrangements and reciprocal communication routes with local partners. Attend local partnership forums and contribute to coordinated support around Confident Futures participants. Adviser and coach support Provide factual advice to EAs and Health Confidence Coaches about local services, referral routes and access barriers. Contribute to Health Confidence Case Reviews where system barriers are delaying progress. Help identify alternatives where services are delayed, unavailable, unsuitable or declined. Support teams to understand local gaps, pathway changes and community opportunities. Long-term condition, disability and accessibility navigation Use enhanced knowledge of long-term and fluctuating conditions, disability, neurodiversity and mental wellbeing barriers to understand functional and participation impacts. Identify environmental and accessibility barriers such as transport, digital exclusion, communication needs, appointment format, confidence and local provision gaps. Support reasonable adjustment conversations and practical access planning without providing clinical advice. Safeguarding and escalation support Recognise, respond to and escalate safeguarding, crisis or urgent concerns in line with Maximus policy and local pathways. Maintain accurate documentation of concerns, information shared, actions taken and outcomes. Operate with Safeguarding Adults Level 3 training and access to role-specific safeguarding supervision. Liaise with the Safeguarding Lead and Clinical Governance Lead where concerns exceed role scope. Continuous improvement and reporting Identify recurring access problems, referral gaps, waiting-list issues and local service capacity barriers. Monitor referral outcomes and support evidence for performance, participant experience and quarterly reporting. Feed local intelligence into continuous improvement, partnership development and solution design. Support quality assurance through accurate, timely and auditable records. Experience building partnerships and developing referral pathways with external agencies. Knowledge of long-term conditions, fluctuating conditions, mental wellbeing barriers, neurodiversity, disability and health inequalities. Understanding of safeguarding, consent, confidentiality, information sharing and professional boundaries. Desirable Experience as a social prescribing link worker, community connector, health navigator, care coordinator, employment specialist or partnership officer Experience of Restart, IPES, IPS, supported employment or integrated health and employment programmes Health or social care background in a non-clinical navigation capacity. This position operates on a four-day work week, consisting of 8-hour shifts on Fridays and Mondays, and 12-hour shifts on Saturdays and Sundays — with weekend shift hours specifically structured to align with and provide a seamless hand-off from Cboe's US-based weekend operations team. The role carries direct ownership of Incident Management during the Singapore weekend shift window, including incident triage, escalation, stakeholder communication, and post-incident documentation — ensuring that production events occurring outside of standard weekday coverage windows are handled with the same rigor and urgency as those during the core trading week. The Singapore-based OSC Specialist is responsible for providing first-level world-class support in conjunction with solving problems, monitoring systems, and ensuring platforms maintain a healthy state — troubleshooting when they do not. Individuals in this role will act as a liaison between different stakeholders including global and regional banks, buy-side firms, corporates, prime brokers, and vendors, along with internal business and technology teams. An OSC Specialist must be able to work independently with little to no direct supervision in performing their duties and will have many opportunities to provide input into the full lifecycle of projects and to directly impact the success of the Singapore team and the greater organization. Based on follow-the-sun coverage needs, work schedules may need to adjust throughout the year during daylight savings time to provide for overlapping support schedules with other regions. Major Job Duties Incident Management — Weekend Ownership: Own the Incident Management function during the Singapore weekend shift. Lead incident triage, root cause analysis, escalation, and stakeholder communication for all production events affecting Cboe platforms — including Cboe Global Indices, Data Vantage, and Cboe Titanium — during the weekend coverage window. Ensure timely and accurate incident documentation, drive escalation to on-call engineering and senior operations staff as warranted, and complete post-incident records to support root cause analysis and remediation tracking during the following business week. System Monitoring & Platform Health — Cboe Global Indices: Serve as the primary operational monitor for the Cboe Global Indices platform during the Singapore weekend shift. Perform health checks, review audit logs to verify system changes, and ensure platforms are operating as expected on a 24x7 basis. Monitor database health tools and batch processing pipelines. Take direct action to resolve known issues and escalate novel issues through appropriate channels. Platform Monitoring Growth — Data Vantage & Titanium: Rapidly develop platform familiarity and monitoring capability across Cboe's Data Vantage suite of products (e.g., Hanweck, LiveVol, Silexx, Indices, DataShop) and Cboe Titanium global market platforms. Provide monitoring coverage and supplementary operational support for these platforms during the weekend shift as proficiency is established, contributing to continuous coverage across Cboe's full platform portfolio. US Hand-Off Coordination: Execute structured hand-off processes at the start and end of each weekend shift — receiving the operational status, open incidents, and outstanding items from the US-based weekend team at shift start, and providing a complete, documented status handover to the incoming team at shift end. Ensure continuity of awareness and action across the US-to-Singapore and Singapore-to-US transitions. Technical Support & Troubleshooting: Perform analytical functions to troubleshoot and explain complex technical and/or data issues, conduct root cause analysis and impact analysis, and resolve customer and platform issues related to Cboe's APIs (market data, order entry, web service). Utilize Linux file systems to access system files and directories as part of troubleshooting and resolution. Data Analysis & Reporting: Utilize SQL to conduct data mining against databases, a UNIX shell to examine log files, and Cboe proprietary tools to gather and analyze data, provide reports, and service the needs of customers and business teams. Leverage experience with file transfer processing and cloud technology (e.g., AWS) as applicable. Provide timely and professional outbound communications (internal and external) servicing OSC support queues and providing customer phone support to the "Deliver Plus One" standard. Draft technical notices and updates to technical specifications as required. This role is the primary point of operational ownership during the Singapore weekend shift and serves as a critical communication bridge between Cboe's Singapore presence and its US-based operations team. The ability to communicate clearly and precisely in English — including during incident management, US hand-off coordination, and customer support scenarios — is essential to maintaining continuous and effective operations across the weekend coverage window. Mandarin Chinese fluency is highly desirable . Korean fluency is desirable . Japanese fluency is desirable . Cboe offers trading across a diverse range of products in multiple asset classes and geographies, including options, futures, U.S. and European equities, and FX markets.
